newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Stad Rotterdam link with Amersfoortse to boost EPS.
newsitem.headline: Stad Rotterdam link with Amersfoortse to boost EPS.

text.p: Medium-sized Dutch insurer Stad Rotterdam said on Friday its planned venture with De Amersfoortse would have a good effect on the group's earnings per share.
"If we plan a deal it should be good for shareholders," chairman Carlo de Swart told Reuters in an interview, adding the impact on earnings per share was expected to be good.

Earlier today, Stad Rotterdam said it was in talks with the Muenchener Rueckversicherungs and the Nuernberger Beteiligungs AG to acquire the remaining 45 percent of fellow insurer De Amersfoortse. Stad Rotterdam already owns 55 percent.

It plans to form a new company, to be called ASR Verzekeringsgroep NV, which will include all the shares of both Stad Rotterdam and De Amersfoortse and envisages a stock market listing for the new combination.
Stad Rotterdam posted turnover of 4.0 billion guilders in 1995 and net profits of 133.4 million guilders.
The 1996 results will be published on April 10, 1997.
De Amersfoortse 1996 turnover was about 1.15 billion guilders and profits were expected to be about 15 percent higher than the 53.2 million guilders for 1995, the firm said earlier.
De Swart would not say whether it would issue new shares to pay for the 45 percent stake in De Amersfoortse.
"There are three possibilities," De Swart said. "Either we pay in cash, or we pay in shares or it could be a combination of the two," he said.
"But, we are still in talks (with the Muenchener and Nuernberger)," he said, adding the price was not yet clear.

The planned increase in Stad Rotterdam's stake in De Amersfoortse will have no extra effect on the group's turnover as the total turnover of De Amersfoortse was already consolidated in the group's figures.
But it will have an effect on the group's earnings as only 55 percent of De Amersfoortse profits were taken into account.
The formation of the new venture with De Amersfoortse was likely to be finalised before or during the summer, Stad Rotterdam said.
"We expect to give more details on the deal at the beginning of May," De Swart said.
De Swart said that Stad Rotterdam intended to grow further in its Dutch base and it did not rule out further acquisitions.
"But we are not in talks with other parties at the moment," he said.
If Stad Rotterdam did make a new acquisition the slight preference would for a life insurer.
